- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underreacts to sharp price spikes in true outcomes; fails to anticipate sudden upward moves.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overcorrects after minor price drops, underestimating subsequent rebounds.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days in the early part of the horizon, especially for medium-to-long-term predictions.
- Model overestimates volatility in low-price regimes, leading to excessive upward bias when prices are near support levels.
- Forecasts show diminishing accuracy as horizon extends beyond 15 days — model drifts toward conservative, flat predictions.
- Model fails to capture “rebound after correction” patterns — underestimates price recovery after sharp drops.
- Model overfits recent low-price data, leading to persistent underestimation of true price peaks.
- Model does not adjust for seasonal or event-driven price surges (e.g., policy changes, emissions caps) unless explicitly triggered.
